newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Trade in SKB to be halted for stock split.
newsitem.headline: Trade in SKB to be halted for stock split.

text.p: Trading in Slovenia's second largest bank SKB will be suspended on Friday and Monday due to the bank's stock split, SKB said on Thursday.
The bank will split each share, currently with a nominal value of 20,000 tolars ($128), into 20 new shares with a nominal value of 1,000 tolars each.

The bank said the split would be undertaken in order to make it easier for small shareholders to buy its shares and also to bring the nominal value of shares and global depositary receipts (GDRs) into line.
In February, SKB became the first Slovenian company to be traded abroad, listing its GDRs on the London, Frankfurt and Munich stock exchanges, with 20 GDRs representing one share.
By 0910 GMT on Thursday SKB had jumped 5.75 percent to 45,800 tolars and traders traced the gains to the stock split making the share cheaper to buy.
They said the share could rise to about 50,000 tolars over the next week, which would translate into 2,500 tolars per new share.
